the high human density and intense land use in the peri-urban area around the reserve, together with the proximity to the city of Santiago, are the main drivers for a high propagule pressure by aliens and their establishment in the reserve.
the richness of alien species was positively associated to the amount of anthropogenic disturbance, whereas the richness of native species was negatively affected by alien species richness.
the richness of alien plant species in this reserve was positively associated to the proportion of alien-dominated forests and the proximity to ruderal and road habitats.

the question how peri-urban reserves can be managed to preserve their biodiversity.
the question of what factors determine invasibility of peri-urban reserves.
the conservation of native plant species in peri-urban reserves and provides important insights for the conservation of biodiversity in highly anthropogenic landscapes.

the peri-urban reserve under investigation is a biodiversity hotspot, but it is threatened by alien species and their spread into native forest areas.

in order to prevent the further spread of invasive species into peri- urban reserves, large-scale anthropogenic disturbances should minimized, already invaded areas should be monitored, and buffer-zones should be established to protect reserves from surrounding land-use activities.
